q: Fischer's canonical automaton for a sofic shift S gives the minimal right-resolving presentation. An edge-labeled graph (G, L) presents S if the labeling is right-resolving, meaning:
opts: Each vertex has exactly one outgoing edge per label
The in-degree of each vertex equals its out-degree
The labeling uses the full alphabet
exp: Right-resolving: at each vertex, each label appears on at most one outgoing edge. This means the path reading a word w starting from a fixed vertex is uniquely determined by w. The Fischer cover is the minimal right-resolving presentation of a sofic shift.
